ei.title: A Band United by a Name
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: My name is Lee Saem. My first name has an impressive meaning in Korean: “a source of power and vitality.” Since Saem sounds like Sam, I decided to make that my English name. Growing up, I thought Lee was a common last name only in Korea. Little did I know that it’s actually common in many other countries, too. When I searched “Sam Lee” on a social media website, I was amazed at what I saw. There were so many people all over the world with that name! Just for fun, I randomly chose several Sam Lees and sent them friend requests. An Unexpected Connection A lot of them accepted my friend request. While looking through their profiles, I noticed something interesting. Several Sam Lees of various ages and nationalities were interested in music. There was a Sam Lee in his mid-30s from Singapore who enjoyed singing and writing lyrics. And there was a 42-year-old Canadian Sam Lee who was a drummer. According to her profile, everyone called her Sam even though her real name was Samantha. Finally, there was an American Sam Lee who played the electric guitar. Suddenly, I had a great idea. I sent a message to all three. Here is what I wrote: “Hi! I’m Sam Lee from Korea. I write songs and play the keyboard. How about making a virtual band called The Sam Lees?” To my surprise, all three eagerly agreed. That was the start of our band’s journey. The Virtual Music Factory We tried to practice once a week through a video chat app, but we encountered several problems. First of all, we all lived in different time zones. This made it difficult to pick a convenient time for everyone to practice. Secondly, there were audio issues with the app, which caused us to be out of sync. So we put our heads together and devised a better way of playing music. We decided to assemble the songs as if we were working in a virtual music factory. After we decided on a song, I would play it on my keyboard and send it to Singaporean Sam. He would sing along with the keyboard and send the recording to American Sam. Then American Sam would add his guitar part, and Samantha would finish the song with her drumming. When it came to choosing songs to play, we took turns. Since each of us prefers a different genre of music and comes from a different culture, we all ended up learning a lot about different kinds of music. It was interesting and a lot of fun. “Long-Distance Friendship” Shortly after we started the band, a global pandemic* began. Since all of our normal lives were put on hold, we valued our online interactions more than ever. At one point, Singaporean Sam became ill and needed to spend some time in the hospital, so the band took a break. However, we still met from time to time by using the video chat app. We talked about our lives and did what we could do to cheer Singaporean Sam up. Since he had to stay in the hospital on his birthday, the rest of us recorded his favorite song as his birthday present. When we played it for him, he laughed so hard that he cried. That was mainly because the song was sung by the worst singer in the band — me! It was good to see him laugh even though he was lying in his hospital bed. After Singaporean Sam recovered, we decided to write and record our own song. We called the song “Long-Distance Friendship,” and we posted it online. The song didn’t get much attention, but we were proud of what we had achieved together. Our band is something really special. Never did we expect that we would build such strong relationships with one another. After all, we don’t come from similar backgrounds, nor have we had the same life experiences. Yet we now talk about almost everything together, including the hardships we face in life. I think it’s been really valuable to get advice from people with such different perspectives. We would all like to meet in person and play our music on the street someday. But even if that never happens, we’ve still been incredibly lucky. Four random people became great friends simply because of our names. Life can be amazing sometimes!

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
① to pick: made it difficult + to부정사(진목적어). 가목적어 it의 진목적어로 to부정사 적절
② playing: a better way of playing music — 전치사 of 뒤 동명사(V-ing) 적절
③ assembling → to assemble: decide는 목적어로 to부정사를 취하는 동사(decide to V). We decided to assemble이 맞음. 동명사 assembling은 부적절 ←정답
④ were working: as if we were working — as if 가정법 과거에서 be동사 were 적절
det.tip: decide는 to부정사만 목적어로 취합니다(decide to V). decide + V-ing는 불가능합니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
① looking: While looking through ~ — 분사구문(While + V-ing) 적절
② were interested: 주어 Several Sam Lees(복수)에 맞는 복수 동사 were 적절
③ called her: everyone called her Sam — call + 목적어 + 목적격보어(SVOC) 구조 적절
④ playing → played: 주격 관계대명사 who의 동사 자리이므로 정동사가 필요. an American Sam Lee who played가 맞음. 현재분사 playing은 정동사가 될 수 없어 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 주격 관계대명사(who) 뒤에는 선행사에 수·시제를 맞춘 정동사가 와야 합니다. 현재분사(V-ing) 단독은 불가합니다.

det.analysis:
① Grew → Growing: 문두의 분사구문 자리. 주절(I thought)의 주어 I와 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 Growing up이 맞음. 과거형 정동사 Grew는 접속사 없이 쓸 수 없어 부적절 ←정답
② what I saw: 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what(=the thing that). at what I saw 적절
③ chose: 과거 시제 문맥(randomly chose)에 맞는 choose의 과거형 적절
④ accepted: A lot of them accepted — 과거 시제 정동사 적절
det.tip: 분사구문은 V-ing(능동)/p.p.(수동) 형태입니다. 접속사 없이 정동사(Grew)를 문두에 둘 수 없습니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
① did we expect: 부정어 Never가 문두에 오면 주어·동사 도치(Never did we expect) 적절
② have we had: nor 뒤에서도 도치가 일어남(nor have we had) 적절
③ to get: it's been valuable to get advice — 가주어 it, 진주어 to부정사 적절
④ happen → happens: even if that never happens에서 주어 that(3인칭 단수)에 맞는 동사 happens가 맞음. happen은 수 일치 위반 ←정답
det.tip: 부정어(Never, nor)가 문두에 오면 도치가 일어납니다. if절 주어 that는 단수이므로 happens가 옳습니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① valued(소중히 여겼다): 평범한 삶이 보류되어 온라인 소통을 소중히 여겼다는 문맥에 적절
② healthy(건강한) → ill(아픈): 병원에서 시간을 보내야 했고 밴드가 휴식을 취했다는 문맥이므로 '아프게 되었다(became ill)'가 맞음. healthy는 정반대 ←정답
③ cheer(격려하다): 싱가포르 Sam을 격려하기 위해 노력했다는 문맥에 적절
④ cried(울었다): 너무 심하게 웃어서 울었다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: 뒤에 이어지는 '병원 입원, 밴드 휴식'이라는 부정적 상황과 어울리는 단어는 ill(아픈)입니다.

questions.passage: First of all, we all lived in different time zones.  This made it ①<u>difficult</u> to pick a convenient time for everyone to practice. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 어려운, 동시에 연주할 수 없는, 버렸다(→고안했다), 조합하다.
det.analysis:
① difficult(어려운): 다른 시간대 때문에 모두에게 편한 시간을 정하기 어려웠다는 문맥에 적절
② out of sync(동시에 연주할 수 없는): 오디오 문제로 박자가 어긋났다는 문맥에 적절
③ abandoned(버렸다) → devised(고안했다): 머리를 맞대고 '더 나은 방법을 고안했다'가 문맥에 맞음. 버렸다는 것은 이후 그 방법을 사용하는 흐름과 모순 ←정답
④ assemble(조합하다): 가상의 음악 공장에서처럼 노래를 조합하기로 했다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: '머리를 맞댔다(put our heads together)' 뒤에는 문제 해결책을 '고안했다(devised)'가 자연스럽습니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 모두가 연습하기에 편한 시간을 정하기 어려웠다.
det.analysis:
① different(다른): 시간의 편의성을 나타내지 못함
② normal(평범한): 연습 시간의 성격과 어울리지 않음
③ similar(비슷한): 모두에게 맞는 시간의 조건으로 부적절
④ convenient(편리한): 서로 다른 시간대 때문에 모두에게 '편한' 시간을 정하기 어려웠다는 흐름에 적절 ←정답
det.tip: 다른 시간대(different time zones)라는 단서로 보아 모두에게 convenient(편리한) 시간을 정하기 어려웠음을 추론할 수 있습니다.

det.korean: 다른 관점을 가진 사람들에게서 조언을 얻는 것이 소중했다.
det.analysis:
① money(돈): 서로 다른 관점에서 얻는 것으로 부적절
② rest(휴식): 문맥과 무관
③ advice(조언): 서로 다른 관점(different perspectives)을 가진 사람들에게서 '조언'을 얻는 것이 소중했다는 흐름에 적절 ←정답
④ fame(명성): 우정과 조언을 강조하는 문맥과 어울리지 않음
det.tip: different perspectives(다른 관점)를 가진 사람들에게서 얻어 valuable한 것은 advice(조언)입니다.

questions.passage: Suddenly, I had a great idea.  I sent a message to all three.  Here is what I wrote: “Hi!  I’m Sam Lee from Korea.  I write songs and play the keyboard.  How about making a virtual band called The Sam Lees?
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 글쓴이(Sam Lee)가 밴드에서 직접 연주하는 악기가 무엇인지 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 본문 'I write songs and play the keyboard.'에서 글쓴이는 곡을 쓰고 keyboard(키보드)를 연주한다고 밝혔다.
det.tip: play the keyboard(키보드를 연주하다)에서 글쓴이의 악기를 확인할 수 있습니다.

questions.passage: So we put our heads together and devised a better way of playing music.  We decided to assemble the songs as if we were working in a virtual music factory.  After we decided on a song, I would play it on my keyboard and send it to Singaporean Sam.  He would sing along with the keyboard and send the recording to American Sam.  Then American Sam would add his guitar part, and Samantha would finish the song with her drumming.  When it came to choosing songs to play, we took turns.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 밴드 멤버들이 노래를 조합하는 작업 방식을 어떤 곳에 비유했는지 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (3단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 본문 'We decided to assemble the songs as if we were working in a virtual music factory.'에서 노래를 조합하는 작업을 virtual music factory(가상의 음악 공장)에서 일하는 것에 비유했다.
det.tip: as if we were working in ~ (마치 ~에서 일하는 것처럼)이 비유 표현입니다.

questions.passage: After Singaporean Sam recovered, we decided to write and record our own song. The song didn't get much attention, but we were proud of what we had __________ (achieve) together.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: '우리가 함께 이룬 것'이라는 의미가 되도록 achieve를 변형.
det.analysis: 구문 분석: what we had ___ together는 관계대명사 what절이며, had 뒤에는 과거완료(had + p.p.)를 이루는 과거분사가 필요하다. achieve의 과거분사는 achieved이므로 had achieved(이루었다)가 맞다.
det.tip: had 다음에는 과거분사(p.p.)가 와서 과거완료를 만듭니다. achieve → achieved.

questions.passage: My name is Lee Saem.  My first name has an impressive meaning in Korean: “a source of power and vitality. ” Since Saem sounds like Sam, I decided to make that my English name.  Growing up, I thought Lee was a common last name only in Korea.  Little did I know that it’s actually common in many other countries, too.  When I searched “Sam Lee” on a social media website, I was amazed at what I saw.  There were so many people all over the world with that name!  Just for fun, I randomly chose several Sam Lees and sent them friend requests.  An Unexpected Connection A lot of them accepted my friend request.  While looking through their profiles, I noticed something interesting.  Several Sam Lees of various ages and nationalities were interested in music.  There was a Sam Lee in his mid-30s from Singapore who enjoyed singing and writing lyrics.  And there was a 42-year-old Canadian Sam Lee who was a drummer.  According to her profile, everyone called her Sam even though her real name was Samantha.  Finally, there was an American Sam Lee who played the electric guitar.  Suddenly, I had a great idea.  I sent a message to all three.  Here is what I wrote: “Hi!  I’m Sam Lee from Korea.  I write songs and play the keyboard.  How about making a virtual band called The Sam Lees? ” To my surprise, all three eagerly agreed.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① 같은 이름(Sam Lee)을 가진 낯선 사람들이 소셜 미디어로 만나 The Sam Lees라는 밴드를 결성한 이야기가 글의 중심 소재 ←정답
② 소셜 미디어의 부정적 영향은 다루지 않음
③ 성공한 음악가의 조건은 글의 주제가 아님
④ 유행병의 산업적 영향은 언급되지 않음
det.tip: 주제는 글 전체를 포괄해야 합니다. 세부 소재가 아닌 중심 내용을 골라야 합니다.

ch: 이름이 같은 낯선 사람들이 온라인으로 만나 밴드를 결성하게 된 이야기
소셜 미디어가 청소년의 일상에 미치는 부정적인 영향
성공한 음악가가 되기 위해 반드시 갖춰야 할 조건들
전 세계적 유행병이 대중음악 산업에 가져온 변화

questions.passage: Our band is something really special.  Never did we expect that we would build such strong relationships with one another.  After all, we don’t come from similar backgrounds, nor have we had the same life experiences.  Yet we now talk about almost everything together, including the hardships we face in life.  I think it’s been really valuable to get advice from people with such different perspectives.  We would all like to meet in person and play our music on the street someday.  But even if that never happens, we’ve still been incredibly lucky.  Four random people became great friends simply because of our names.  Life can be amazing sometimes!
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① 온라인 소통이 대면을 '완전히 대체'한다는 내용은 없음(오히려 언젠가 직접 만나고 싶어 함)
② 비슷한 배경이 아니어도(don't come from similar backgrounds) 이름이라는 공통점으로 값진 우정을 쌓았다는 것이 핵심 메시지 ←정답
③ 뛰어난 재능이 있어야만 밴드를 만들 수 있다는 내용은 없음(글쓴이는 최악의 가수)
④ 관심을 못 받아도 함께 이룬 것을 자랑스러워했으므로 '가치가 없다'는 정반대
det.tip: 요지는 글쓴이의 핵심 주장입니다. 마지막 문단의 우정에 대한 태도에 주목하세요.

ch: 온라인 소통은 대면 만남을 완전히 대체할 수 있다.
서로 다른 배경을 가진 사람들도 공통점을 통해 값진 우정을 쌓을 수 있다.
음악적 재능이 뛰어난 사람들만이 좋은 밴드를 만들 수 있다.
널리 알려지지 못한 음악은 만든 이에게 아무런 가치가 없다.

questions.passage: Suddenly, I had a great idea.  I sent a message to all three.  Here is what I wrote: “Hi!  I’m Sam Lee from Korea.  __________.  How about making a virtual band called The Sam Lees?
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'나는 곡을 쓰고 키보드를 연주한다.'

[조건]
(1) I, and, keyboard, play, songs, the, write를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 글쓴이가 자신의 음악 활동을 소개하는 문장.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- I(주어) + write(동사) + songs(목적어): 나는 곡을 쓴다
- and(등위접속사) + play(동사) + the keyboard(목적어): 그리고 키보드를 연주한다
- 하나의 주어 I에 write와 play 두 동사가 and로 병렬 연결된 구조
det.tip: 등위접속사 and가 write songs와 play the keyboard 두 동사구를 병렬로 연결합니다.

questions.wa: I write songs and play the keyboard
